title: Microsoft Purview: recurring classifier refresh for existing content
summary: Hold: the endpoint billing advice omits the Windows-update and prior-classification conditions needed to avoid repeat charges. The briefing also extends a results timetable and existing scan controls beyond their documented scope, and attributes rule settings to the scan-creation cmdlet.

claims.quote: Evolve On-Demand Classification into recurring classification refreshes

claims.claim: The planned refreshes help keep existing content classification current as data and context change.
claims.quote: help keep existing content classification current as data and context change.

claims.quote: During this process, you define the following settings: ... Classifiers to scan for

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Today's documented portal workflow starts classification when an administrator selects Start classification after estimation.
claims.quote: From the On-demand classification list view, select the scan you created. ... Select View estimation. ... Select Start classification.

claims.claim: Updated SharePoint and OneDrive classification results can trigger active matching policies, including applying or removing sensitivity labels.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Running an existing on-demand scan requires membership in the Compliance Administrator role group.
claims.quote: To run a scan, you must be a member of the following role group: Compliance Administrator

claims.claim: Viewing classification results requires Content Explorer Content Viewer or Content Explorer List Viewer membership.
claims.quote: To view classification results, you must be a member of one of these role groups: Content Explorer Content Viewer; Content Explorer List Viewer

claims.claim: Results from the scans just described, including endpoint scans, appear in Content Explorer within seven days.
claims.quote: Searched: '"on-demand classification" "Content Explorer" "seven" endpoints'; opened on-demand-classification and on-demand-classification-endpoints. The seven-day statement is under SharePoint and OneDrive; no endpoint timetable was found.
claims.fix: Replace 'Results appear in Content Explorer within seven days' with 'For SharePoint and OneDrive scans, Content Explorer updates within seven days of scanning', retaining the existing role requirement. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/on-demand-classification#additional-considerations.

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes can bound today's SharePoint on-demand scans dynamically.
claims.quote: Adaptive scopes for SharePoint on-demand classification let administrators define scan scope dynamically based on site attributes (such as URL, name, or metadata) instead of selecting sites manually.

claims.claim: Administrative units can bound and delegate today's SharePoint on-demand scans.
claims.quote: Administrators can create and manage scans only for sites within their assigned AUs, and access to scan configuration and results is limited to AU-scoped admins.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Scanned files are evaluated against DLP, Information Protection, Data Lifecycle Management and Insider Risk Management policies.
claims.quote: Each file, once scanned, is evaluated against Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Information Protection (MIP), Data Lifecycle Management (DLM), and Insider Risk Management (IRM) policies, triggering appropriate actions as per matching policies.

claims.claim: Selecting specific classifiers updates only their results and may leave other classifiers' policies untriggered.
claims.quote: If you select specific classifiers during a scan, only those classifiers have their classification results updated for the scanned files. Other classifiers present in the files might remain unevaluated and might not trigger their associated policies.

claims.claim: A location in scope of several active scans is processed by only one.
claims.quote: Applies to SharePoint and OneDrive ... If a location is in scope of multiple active scans, only one scan processes it successfully and marks it skipped for others.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'For SharePoint and OneDrive, a location in scope of several active scans is processed by only one and marked skipped for the others.' This preserves the documented workload qualification.

claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive scan can process up to 150,000 locations.
claims.quote: Applies to SharePoint and OneDrive ... Each scan can process up to 150,000 locations and 100 million files.

claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive scan can process up to 100 million files.
claims.quote: Applies to SharePoint and OneDrive ... Each scan can process up to 150,000 locations and 100 million files.

claims.claim: Learn warns that EDM classifiers cause previously classified files to be rescanned, potentially increasing scan costs.
claims.quote: Tenants using EDM classifiers should be aware that On-Demand Classification scans (including estimation and classification) rescan previously classified files, which can increase overall scan costs.

claims.claim: A billing rule or rate specific to recurring refreshes, including repeat billing for unchanged files, is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview recurring classifier refresh licensing billing rate roles scope default'; opened purview-billing-models, on-demand-classification and endpoints-faq-reference. These describe current scan billing, not recurring-refresh-specific rates or repeat-billing rules.

claims.claim: Endpoint scan estimation is not billed.
claims.quote: Is estimation billed? No. Estimation is a metadata-only pass. ... No charges are incurred during estimation.

claims.claim: Unchanged endpoint files with the same classifiers are not rescanned or billed, without further qualifications.
claims.quote: Reuse of previously classified verdicts requires that the earlier scan used advanced classification. ... The device has the latest Windows cumulative updates installed. ... Scans completed before this update aren't eligible.
claims.fix: Replace the endpoint no-rebilling clause with: 'On endpoints, unchanged files with unchanged classifiers are not rescanned or billed when the earlier classification used advanced classification and the device has the latest Windows cumulative updates. Recognition is not retroactive: the first scan after the required update establishes the baseline.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoints-best-practices alongside the FAQ.

claims.claim: The existing scan-creation UI is Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Classifiers > On-demand classification > New scan.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Go to Data loss prevention > Classifiers > On-demand classification ... Select New scan.

claims.claim: New-SensitiveInformationScan -Name <name> -SharePointLocation All creates an on-demand scan scoped to all SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Use the New-SensitiveInformationScan cmdlet to create new on-demand classification scans. ... The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the scan. ... you can use the value All to include all sites.

claims.claim: Set-SensitiveInformationScan -Identity <scan> -CancelScan $true cancels an active classification scan.
claims.quote: The CancelScan parameter specifies whether to cancel an active scan in the classification stage. ... $true: Cancel the active scan. ... The Identity parameter specifies the sensitive information scan that you want to modify.

claims.claim: The documented New-SensitiveInformationScan and Set-SensitiveInformationScan commands are available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The scan-creation cmdlet, like the wizard, documents classifier selection, date range and file-extension settings.
claims.quote:
New-SensitiveInformationScan "SharePoint scan" -SharePointLocation All

New-SensitiveInformationScanRule "SharePoint scan rule" -ContentExtensionMatchesWords "pdf", "docx" -Policy "SharePoint scan" -Workload SharePoint
claims.fix: Replace 'The scan wizard and cmdlet document scope, classifiers, date range and file extensions, but neither documents a schedule' with 'The scan wizard documents scope, classifiers, date range and file extensions. Neither the wizard nor New-SensitiveInformationScan documents a schedule.' The creation cmdlet's syntax lacks the rule-setting parameters; its example uses a separate New-SensitiveInformationScanRule operation.

claims.claim: A policy being tested can remain in simulation while other active policies act on reclassified files.
claims.quote: Before starting classification for SharePoint or OneDrive, review the scan scope, estimated charges, and active policies that might act on the updated results. ... A policy you're testing can remain in simulation while other active policies act on those files.

claims.claim: The Items for review tab shows specific items found during an existing scan.
claims.quote: On the Items for review tab, review specific items found during the scan. You can filter and export the result.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: A first recurring refresh can be scoped using specific SharePoint sites or adaptive scopes and a selected classifier list.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview recurring classifier refresh licensing billing rate roles scope default' and '"recurring classifier refresh" "Purview"'; opened on-demand-classification. Specific sites, classifiers and adaptive scopes are documented for today's scans, not confirmed for recurring refreshes.
claims.fix: Replace the first At rollout bullet with 'Confirm whether recurring refresh supports specific SharePoint sites, adaptive scopes and classifier selection before choosing a pilot scope.' This keeps the advice without asserting an undocumented control applies.

claims.quote: Searched: '"recurring classifier refresh" "Purview"'; read the roadmap, on-demand-classification and New-/Set-SensitiveInformationScan syntax. No recurring-refresh review workflow was documented.

claims.claim: Several checklist controls lack corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: List the active DLP, auto-labeling, retention and Insider Risk Management policies ... Keep policies you are still testing in simulation ... Record which role group members can create scans ... Review the Items for review tab and Content Explorer
claims.fix: The Before rollout policy-inventory and Azure-subscription-association steps, At rollout simulation-mode and role-group-inventory steps, and After rollout Content Explorer review step have no corresponding control rows. The existing rows cover scan creation, recurrence, usage pausing and scan cancellation only.
